title: 家事支援やベビーシッター利用で税制優遇、政府が調整…共働き世帯の負担軽減
extracted_text:
政府は、家事支援サービスやベビーシッターの普及を後押しするため、利用者への税制優遇制度を新設する方向で調整に入った。共働き世帯などの経済的負担を和らげ、家庭と仕事の両立を下支えする狙いがある。年末にまとめる政府・与党の税制改正大綱に具体策を盛り込む方向だ。
佐藤啓官房副長官が３０日、高市内閣発足から半年が過ぎたのに合わせて読売新聞のインタビューに応じ、明らかにした。
佐藤氏は「ベビーシッターと家事支援サービスの利用支援に向け、税負担を軽減する」と明言した上で、需要が増えた場合のサービスの担い手不足といった課題を年末までに洗い出すと説明した。「税負担の軽減」は、利用代金の一部を納税額から差し引く税額控除などの手法が想定される。
共働き世帯では、家事や育児の負担が今なお女性に集中し、離職などの弊害を招いている。２０２７年に予定する家事支援サービスの国家資格創設と合わせ、国主導でサービス普及に力を入れることで、女性の働きにくさ解消を目指す。
佐藤氏は、企業が従業員らの子どもを預かる「企業内学童保育」を支援する考えも示し、具体的な需要を調査中だと明らかにした。小学生になった子どもを夏休みなどに預ける先がない「小１の壁」が問題化していることが背景にある。子どもの自殺対策も強化すると述べ、「弱い立場の人々を含め、幅広い国民の声を拾い、政策のウィングを広げていく」と強調した。
（詳しくはこちら）
translated_text: The government has begun coordinating to establish a new tax incentive system for users in order to promote the spread of housekeeping support services and babysitters. The aim is to alleviate the economic burden on dual-income households and other families, and support the balancing of family and work. Specific measures will be incorporated into the government's tax reform outline to be compiled by the end of the year with the ruling party. Chief Cabinet Secretary Saito responded to a Yomiuri Shimbun interview on the 30th, marking half a year since the Kishida cabinet was formed, to announce this. Saito clearly stated, "We will reduce the tax burden to support the use of babysitters and housekeeping services," while also explaining that the government will identify issues such as a shortage of service providers by the end of the year, in case demand increases. "Tax burden reduction" is expected to involve methods such as tax credits that allow part of the service fees to be deducted from the tax amount owed. In dual-income households, housekeeping and childcare responsibilities remain disproportionately on women, leading to issues such as women leaving their jobs. Along with the planned creation of a national qualification for housekeeping services in 2027, the government aims to address the challenges women face in the workplace by promoting the spread of these services under government leadership. Saito also expressed the government's intention to support "corporate childcare" where companies provide childcare for their employees' children, stating that a concrete demand survey is underway. This is against the backdrop of the so-called "first-grade wall" problem, where parents have no place to entrust their children during summer breaks and other school vacations. Saito emphasized the need to strengthen suicide prevention measures for children, stating, "We will broaden the scope of our policies to capture the voices of a wide range of citizens, including those in vulnerable positions."
title_en: Government to Introduce Tax Breaks for Housekeeping Services and Babysitters to Ease Burden on Dual-Income Households
